findings.title: HuggingFace transformers vulnerable to remote code execution

normalized_input.claimed_source: attacker-controlled model config.json or HuggingFace model repository
normalized_input.claimed_sink: model initialization that downloads and executes attacker-controlled Python kernel code
preconditions: The local MinerU process loads a model configuration containing an attacker-controlled _attn_implementation_internal value
The affected Transformers model-loading path is reached
normalized_input.impact: arbitrary code execution with the local operator process privileges

affected_locations.label: optional dependency
affected_locations.detail: The local ingestion extra pins MinerU with both pipeline and VLM support.

affected_locations.label: locked vulnerable dependency
affected_locations.detail: MinerU pipeline and VLM extras bring in Transformers; the lock resolves Transformers 4.57.6 at lines 1892-1893.

affected_locations.label: local model acquisition
affected_locations.detail: The operator downloads MinerU model artifacts from HuggingFace once and then selects the local model source.

affected_locations.label: local CLI boundary
affected_locations.detail: The repository invokes the pinned MinerU executable as a local subprocess.

reachable_path: A trusted operator downloads the MinerU model set from HuggingFace
The local ingestion CLI launches MinerU with pipeline or VLM support
The hash-matched MinerU 3.4.5 wheel contains Transformers from_pretrained model-loading calls, including a causal-language-model registration path
Whether a downloaded model config can reach the advisory's dynamic-kernel path is not proven by repository-static evidence

boundary_assessment.policy_basis: SECURITY.md permits authorized local ingest but treats model and external artifacts as bounded supply-chain inputs; the local ingestion runbook downloads model artifacts from HuggingFace

exploitability_stack_rank.rationale: This is the only alert with a plausible static bridge from the locked dependency to MinerU model initialization and an external model-artifact boundary.

evidence: The lock resolves Transformers 4.57.6, which is inside the advisory range below 5.3.0.
The runbook downloads the MinerU model set from HuggingFace and then runs those artifacts locally.

The exact MinerU 3.4.5 wheel matched lockfile SHA-256 4a73b865920bb9109c1b8b1bc46567e296bf0133a67106a04effd219536ae72d and contains multiple from_pretrained calls plus an AutoModelForCausalLM registration.
counterevidence: Repository code accepts a policy-document root, not an arbitrary model repository identifier.
The documented steady-state extraction path sets MINERU_MODEL_SOURCE=local.
No repository code sets _attn_implementation_internal or trust_remote_code.
proof_gaps: The repository does not record the downloaded model repository revisions or content digests.
Static evidence does not prove whether the selected MinerU models exercise the exact vulnerable dynamic-kernel branch.
A compatible MinerU or Transformers upgrade has not been qualified against the extraction configuration and existing 236 bundles.
findings.recommended_next_step: Pin and verify the exact MinerU model revisions or digests, confirm the affected model-loading branch against those artifacts, and design a compatible upgrade to Transformers 5.3.0 or later through a qualified MinerU release.

findings.title: Arbitrary code execution in the Transformers LightGlue model loading path

normalized_input.claimed_source: attacker-controlled LightGlue model repository and serialized configuration
normalized_input.claimed_sink: nested AutoConfig.from_pretrained call that executes attacker-provided Python
normalized_input.claimed_control: trust_remote_code=false is overridden by untrusted nested configuration
preconditions: The LightGlue model repository or config is attacker-controlled
normalized_input.impact: arbitrary code execution with the local operator process privileges

affected_locations.label: locked dependency
affected_locations.detail: Transformers is present only through the optional MinerU pipeline and VLM extras.

affected_locations.label: documented model boundary
affected_locations.detail: The documented operator path downloads MinerU's model set and selects local models.

boundary_assessment.policy_basis: The local ingestion runbook defines a fixed MinerU model workflow; repository and hash-matched MinerU 3.4.5 source contain no LightGlue reference or LightGlue model selection surface.

evidence: The locked Transformers version falls inside the advisory range.
counterevidence: No LightGlue reference exists in repository code or documentation.
No LightGlue reference exists in the exact hash-matched MinerU 3.4.5 wheel.
The CLI exposes a policy source folder and MinerU backend choice, not a caller-selected model repository.
proof_gaps: The separately downloaded model artifacts are outside the repository and were not inspected.
findings.recommended_next_step: Record this scoped rationale before any dismissal and re-triage if MinerU adds LightGlue or arbitrary model-repository selection.

findings.title: Arbitrary code execution in the Transformers Trainer checkpoint path

normalized_input.claimed_source: malicious Trainer checkpoint file such as rng_state.pth
normalized_input.claimed_control: safe_globals does not protect PyTorch versions below 2.6
preconditions: Transformers Trainer resumes from an attacker-controlled checkpoint
normalized_input.impact: arbitrary code execution with the local operator process privileges

affected_locations.label: local extraction command
affected_locations.detail: The only dependency entrypoint performs MinerU document extraction.

boundary_assessment.policy_basis: The product implements inference-only policy extraction and exposes no model training or Trainer checkpoint-resume workflow.

evidence: Transformers 4.57.6 is present in the lockfile.
counterevidence: Repository code contains no Trainer, training, or rng_state checkpoint call.
The exact hash-matched MinerU 3.4.5 wheel contains no Transformers Trainer reference.
The documented workflow is local document extraction, not model training.
findings.recommended_next_step: Record this scoped rationale before any dismissal and re-triage if a training or Trainer checkpoint workflow is introduced.

findings.title: PyTorch memory corruption through torch.jit.script

preconditions: The local process calls torch.jit.script with exploit-triggering input
normalized_input.impact: bounded local confidentiality, integrity, and availability impact

affected_locations.label: locked dependency
affected_locations.detail: The optional MinerU environment resolves PyTorch 2.8.0.

boundary_assessment.policy_basis: PyTorch exists only in the local optional MinerU environment, and no torch.jit.script sink was found in repository or hash-matched MinerU source.

evidence: PyTorch 2.8.0 is inside the advisory range.
counterevidence: No torch.jit.script call exists in repository code.
No torch.jit.script call exists in the exact hash-matched MinerU 3.4.5 wheel.
The only nearby MinerU occurrence is torch.jit.is_tracing, which is a different API.
proof_gaps: Static inspection did not recursively inspect every package in the 110-package optional environment.
findings.recommended_next_step: Record this scoped rationale before any dismissal and re-triage if a JIT compilation path is added or MinerU changes.
